subject.title: Add auth sync command or auto-sync for API key rotation across agents

question: Should OpenClaw solve env-backed API-key rotation shadowing with an explicit operator-controlled repair/warning path, automatic auth-store sync on config/env writes, or runtime fallback after credential failure?
rationale: Each viable path changes credential copying, auth precedence, or failure recovery across agent stores, which is a security-sensitive auth-provider boundary rather than a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Operator-controlled repair and warning
options.body: Add doctor/status/models-auth detection plus a user-approved repair for shadowed rotated static keys, keeping credential movement explicit and auditable.

options.title: Automatic sync on config/env update
options.body: Propagate supported static keys into affected agent auth stores automatically, accepting a larger silent secret-copying blast radius.

options.title: Runtime fallback after auth failure
options.body: Try env/config credentials after a stored profile fails, accepting a more surprising provider-auth precedence model.

recommendation.title: Operator-controlled repair and warning
recommendation.body: Add doctor/status/models-auth detection plus a user-approved repair for shadowed rotated static keys, keeping credential movement explicit and auditable.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame points to steipete across the central auth resolver and command surfaces, though local history is shallow.
